html:
SMTO-WEB-0055 — SMTO couldn't match a quote to the PDF it came from

GUID: a6290984-c6e5-5db2-a448-7c1bebcf339d
Slug: research-document-provenance-invalid
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • SMTO's answer used text from a PDF, but that text doesn't line up with the exact copy, page or spot in the document SMTO downloaded. So SMTO didn't accept the answer as checked yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let SMTO continue; it should quote the PDF again from the copy it downloaded, or mark that point as unconfirmed. SMTO refused text it couldn't trace to a specific page, so it needs to find the exact passage again.
  2. If the document may have changed online, send a new message asking SMTO to check the PDF again. A fresh check downloads the current version, so quotes match the file SMTO actually has.
  3. Before relying on a quote, open the PDF yourself and find the quoted text. Finding the words in the document confirms the quote really comes from it.

What success looks like

  • The answer quotes PDF pages that SMTO actually read, or clearly says which points it couldn't confirm.

If it still fails

  • If quotes keep being rejected, select Copy error details and send them, with the PDF link, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rely on a quote you couldn't find in the PDF yourself.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof validation rejected a PDF-derived source because its lineage (parent acquisition, document hash, Gateway path, final URL, revision, page, extraction mode or text span) does not match the recorded acquisition and extraction receipts.

What this means

  • PDF lineage cannot match the parent acquisition, document hash, path, final URL, revision, page or exact extraction-span boundaries. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • PDF lineage cannot match the parent acquisition, document hash, path, final URL, revision, page or exact extraction-span boundaries.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare both retained receipts and page offsets instead of attaching a nearby document's provenance.

How to fix it

  • documents.verify_lineage() rejects when the parent DOCUMENT source or document record is missing, or sha256, gateway_path, canonical final URL, document_revision, page_number, extraction_mode or the locator span differ from the retained pdf extraction rows. Inspect the acquisition and PDF receipts, then reacquire or re-extract the exact revision; never carry lineage over from a different or changed document.
  • Inspect the retained acquisition and PDF receipts. Reacquire or inspect the exact document revision; never transfer provenance between documents.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • Each extracted claim resolves to its exact acquired document revision and page.

What not to do

  • Do not substitute a changed PDF under an older source receipt.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
